title: File version history in a single DynamoDB table
name: File version store

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code models and queries file versions in the table? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The version sort key is built as `VER#${n}` with no zero padding. DynamoDB sorts string sort keys lexicographically, so `VER#10` sorts before `VER#9`. Once a file passes version 9, latestVersion (ScanIndexForward: false, Limit: 1) returns VER#9 instead of the real latest, and listVersions returns history out of order. The sync planner then sees remote.version < localBaseVersion and reports conflicts, or tells clients to download a stale version. Padding the number (e.g. VER#0000000010) or using a numeric sort key fixes it.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two clients both read HEAD as version 4 and call commitVersion at the same time. What happens?
choices: Both writes succeed and the later one overwrites version 5
One transaction succeeds; the other is cancelled because its conditions fail, and nothing from it is written
Both transactions fail because DynamoDB transactions cannot touch the same partition
The second client's version item is written but HEAD is not updated
choiceQuestions.explanation: Both try to Put sk VER#5 with attribute_not_exists(pk) and HEAD with version = 4. The first commits; the second's conditions fail and the whole TransactWrite is cancelled atomically, so no partial write remains. Overwriting can't happen because of the conditions, same-partition transactions are allowed, and transactions are all-or-nothing.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why are version items and the HEAD item stored under the same partition key?
choices: So a single Query on pk can retrieve a file's whole history and HEAD can be read with a cheap GetItem on the same key
Because TransactWriteCommand requires all items to share a partition key
To spread writes for a busy file across many partitions
So that deleting HEAD automatically deletes all versions
choiceQuestions.explanation: Grouping items under one pk is the item-collection pattern: Query with begins_with(sk, 'VER#') reads history, and GetItem reads HEAD. Transactions can span different keys and tables, co-locating concentrates rather than spreads writes, and DynamoDB has no cascading deletes.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A file has never been committed. What does commitVersion do when called with expectedHead = 0?
choices: It fails because HEAD does not exist and version = :expected cannot be evaluated
It writes version 0 and a HEAD of 0
It writes VER#1 and creates HEAD with version 1, because attribute_not_exists(pk) passes for the missing HEAD
It writes VER#1 but skips HEAD since no previous HEAD existed
choiceQuestions.explanation: next = 1, and the HEAD condition is 'attribute_not_exists(pk) OR version = :expected'; for a missing item the first clause is true, so both puts succeed. It does not fail, version 0 is never written, and HEAD is always part of the transaction.
